senses.sense_definition: The official act of bringing formal charges of serious misconduct against a public official, often to remove them from office.

examples.text: The legislative committee drafted formal articles of <w>impeachment</w> against the president.
Many citizens gathered to demand the <w>impeachment</w> of the corrupt governor.

senses.sense_definition: The act of challenging or discrediting the integrity, credibility, or accuracy of a witness in a legal proceeding.

examples.text: The defense attorney introduced prior inconsistent statements for the <w>impeachment</w> of the key witness.
Her direct testimony was discredited following an effective <w>impeachment</w> by the prosecutor.

senses.sense_definition: A formal accusation alleging that a person has committed treason or another grave crime against the state.

examples.text: Parliament brought an <w>impeachment</w> of high treason against the minister.
The nobleman fled the country after hearing of his impending <w>impeachment</w>.

senses.sense_definition: The act of challenging, calling into question, or casting doubt on the validity, propriety, or honour of something.

examples.text: His sharp criticism was viewed as an <w>impeachment</w> of their professional judgment.
She rejected any <w>impeachment</w> of her family's honour and reputation.

senses.sense_definition: The condition or state of having been formally accused or impeached.

examples.text: The official remained under <w>impeachment</w> while lawmakers debated the charges.
His sudden resignation spared the administration from prolonged <w>impeachment</w>.

senses.sense_definition: An obstacle, hindrance, or obstruction that prevents free movement or progress.

examples.text: The king granted them safe passage without <w>impeachment</w> across the royal lands.
The soldiers continued their march towards the river without any <w>impeachment</w>.

traits.comment: Used historically to mean hindrance or impediment.
